title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Upper horizontal arrow and left vertical arrow for GL(2) are not injective as literally stated. Aut(GL2) over connected S is PGL2 × Z/2, the extra factor being g ↦ det(g)^{-1}·g (which is transpose-inverse up to an inner automorphism). This automorphism fixes SL2 pointwise, hence fixes ρ0, σ0, ε0, which all have det 1, and it induces the identity on PGL2. So either 'Gl(2)' should be read as SL(2) (consistent with det = 1 in (54)-(56) and with Z/4, Z/6 in (63)), or Isom should be restricted, e.g. to isomorphisms compatible with det. (59) itself (centralizer of ρ and σ in GL2 = scalars) is correct over any base, since the commutant of σ0 and ε0 is visibly the scalars.

(60) appears false over bases where 4 = 0 but 2 ≠ 0, for example S = Spec Z/4. Take g = 1+2ρ0 = [[1,2],[2,3]] in GL2(Z/4) (det = 3, a unit). It commutes with ρ0, and a direct computation gives gσ0g^{-1} = -σ0, so g lies in N'_ρ ∩ N'_σ but is not scalar. Hence Int(g) is a non-trivial automorphism of PGL(2)_{Z/4} fixing (ρ̃0, σ̃0, ε̃0). The lower horizontal arrow of (58) is therefore not injective over Z/4, and the Théorème d'épinglage for PG needs 2 invertible, or must hold only for flat/reduced S or under extra hypotheses. In general the solutions are g = a(1+bρ) with b = -2a and 4a = 0, so the defect is concentrated where 4 = 0 but 2 ≠ 0. Equivalently: the image of SL2(Z) is schematically dense in SL2_Z, but this density does not survive non-flat base change.
Minor point: since Tr ρ = 1, the condition gρg^{-1} = ερ forces ε = 1, so N'_ρ is just the centralizer of ρ. Only N'_σ (Tr σ = 0) genuinely allows ε = -1.

ideas.what: Modular triplets (images of the elliptic generators of order 4 and 6 and the parabolic generator of SL2(Z), linked by -σ^{-1}ρ = ε0) used as a 'pinning' of forms of GL2/PGL2 over an arbitrary base: Isom(GL2,G) ≅ Tripmod(G), Isom(PGL2,PG) ≅ Tripmod(PG)
ideas.modern_name: rigidification/pinning of a reductive group scheme of rank 1 by a homomorphism from SL2(Z) (an analogue of épinglage in SGA3 Exp. XXIII)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pinnings: Chevalley, Demazure-Grothendieck (SGA3). This modular-generator version: not standard; no known attribution
ideas.where_published: Possibly in the unpublished 'Longue Marche' continuation (cote 140-3); the published/transcribed Longue Marche part 1 discusses SL2(Z) and the Teichmüller tower but I am unsure this theorem appears

ideas.what: Injectivity reformulated as: the intersection of the centralizers of ρ and σ in GL2_S is the centre (59), and for PGL2 the intersection of the projective stabilizers N'_ρ ∩ N'_σ is the centre (60)
ideas.modern_name: trivial centralizer / absolute irreducibility of the image of SL2(Z) over every base

missed.claim: The projective half of the 'Théorème d'épinglage' (and the stronger relation (60)) fails over bases with 4 = 0 and 2 ≠ 0. g = 1+2ρ0 in GL2(Z/4) gives a non-trivial automorphism of PGL2_{Z/4} fixing the standard modular triple. The G_a-family ε̃0(λ), not just the section ε̃0(1), is needed to rigidify. This bears directly on the next page's conjectural fpqc presentation of PGL2_Z by Z/2, Z/3, G_a with the single relation (62).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Anyone formalizing Grothendieck's modular-triplet rigidification, or the sheaf-theoretic amalgam question for PGL2_Z/SL2_Z, must handle the 2-adic (mod 4) defect. It shows that the discrete modular group alone does not rigidify the group scheme integrally.

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes characterizing forms of GL2/PGL2 over arbitrary S, and their isomorphisms, purely by modular triplets (an SL2(Z)-based pinning). The idea is tied to the loop equation of the Teichmüller tower but was apparently never written up.
missed.quote: Théorème d'épinglage : Toutes les flèches dans (58) sont bijectives.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a scheme-theoretic, base-independent dictionary between the arithmetic of SL2(Z) (elliptic points of orders 2 and 3, the cusp) and the group scheme PGL2/SL2. This could be relevant to integral/motivic versions of Grothendieck-Teichmüller actions on level structures. Modest novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but fairly elementary rigidification statement using the modular generators as a pinning; not in the literature in this form as far as I know. As stated it has a genuine gap/error (the det-twist automorphism for GL2, and a non-trivial stabilizer over Z/4 for PGL2), which is a notable detail but not a deep result.
transcription_corrections: Top-left '468' is likely an archive/page cross-reference, not mathematics.
'Isom(Gl(2), G)' and 'Isom(GPl(1), PG)': the second group is Grothendieck's GP(1) = PGL(2) (written 'GPU)' in the hand).
'Gl(2)_S = G_0 → G (resp. GPl(1)_S = PG_0 → G)': the second target should read PG.
'Théorème d'épinglage' is a reasonable reading of the underlined heading.
(59): reads 'T_ρ ∩ T_σ = Cent', with a crossed-out symbol before 'Cent'.
'des paragraphes [?] § VI' reads 'du présent § VI' or 'des § VI'; uncertain.
